newsitem.title: UK: Dlr firm but off overnight highs in quiet Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firm but off overnight highs in quiet Europe.

text.p: The dollar was steady against the yen in morning Europe, shrugging off a sharp rise in Japan's current account surplus which came in largely in line with analysts' expectations.
Dollar/mark was firm though off an overnight fresh 41-month high above 1.76 marks, underpinned by sterling's strength against the mark and a subdued economic outlook for Germany.

Japan's May current account surplus rose by 154.9 percent year-on-year, just slightly above an average of analysts' forecasts. The data proved only a limited drag on dollar/yen but helped push mark/yen to a fresh 23-month low.

Although the current account was within expectations and dollar/yen impact limited, analysts said it remains a big political issue and is likely to keep a lid on dollar gains against the yen for the foreseeable future.

"Such a rise would of no consequence if it were not for protectionists in Washington, but political dynamics always dominate while economic ones often do not," said Ken Landon, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Tokyo.
Dollar/yen was trading at 112.81/84 by 0740 GMT, up from an overnight low of 112.40 and just above late Tuesday's European level of 112.72/82 yen.
Mark/yen recovered from a fresh 23-month low of 63.89 seen overnight, now at 64.17/19 against 64.10/15 late Tuesday.

Toyota Motor Corp chief Hiroshi Okuda said early today 110-120 yen was still an appropriate level and added Ford Motor Co vice-chairman Wayne Brooker's earlier call for a range of 100-110 yen per dollar was too high.
Brooker was co-chairing the manufacturing group of a U.S.-Japan business conference in San Francisco.
Dollar/mark was steady, though off a 41-month high overnight of 1.7627. By 0757 GMT it stood at 1.7585/90 against 1.7594/04 late Tuesday in Europe.

"Even though expectations of tightening in the U.S. have waned, there's still problems in Germany as it struggles to get its deficit lower for EMU," said Tom Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.

The German government presents its supplementary budget for 1997 and its budget proposals for 1998 on Friday. Coalition sources said on Tuesday 1998 spending will be above original targets mainly due to high unemployment costs.
This glum German economic backdrop is supportive for the dollar as well as expectations of a broad-based EMU start. This saw the Italian/German 10-year yield spread shrink to new lows.
Sterling/mark, meantime, remained firm amid heightened expectations of an imminent rise in UK interest rates in the wake of Tuesday's strong inflation data.

Although off Tuesday's six-year highs against the mark, the pound was steady around 2.97 with the market focused on the outcome of the two-day Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting which starts today.
Sterling was trading at 2.9698/08 marks against 2.9730/70 late Tuesday in Europe.
